original-rule.implementation: 'ashoka' as a case-folded LITERAL SUBSTRING of the extracted text (answer42's speak default, unchanged, proven by its __defaults__)

new-rule.name: addressing45
new-rule.variant-expansion: FORBIDDEN - the list is closed at freeze time
new-rule.tokenization: tokens = maximal runs of ASCII letters [A-Za-z]+ (re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', text)); every other character is a BOUNDARY
new-rule.case: comparison on token.lower() (ASCII case-fold); the SURFACE spelling is recorded exactly as it appears, never rewritten
new-rule.possessives: the apostrophe is a boundary: "Asoka's" -> tokens 'Asoka', 's' -> MATCHES via its head token; recorded with that fact
new-rule.complete-tokens-only: a variant matches ONLY a whole token: 'Asokan', 'Ashokan', 'asokas' do NOT match (deliberate: no substring false positives)
new-rule.non-ascii: a non-ASCII letter is a boundary; if the held text carries any, the affected tokens are recorded as a limitation rather than normalized
new-rule.no-normalization: no rewriting, transliteration, stemming or diacritic folding of the held text

output-fields.addressed: bool - at least one variant matched at least one complete token
output-fields.counts: per variant, complete-token matches in the held text
output-fields.surfaces: per variant, the exact observed token spellings (with repetitions listed in order of appearance)
output-fields.contexts: for each match, a bounded surrounding window of the ORIGINAL bytes
output-fields.usable: status present AND >= 60 chars AND publisher != the instance house AND addressed
output-fields.experiment-answer: A42's four-word vocabulary reused verbatim: no usable read -> EVIDENCE-GAP; any usable read -> EVIDENCE-BACKED (a read-level word, NOT a corroboration word and NOT a claim about the source's truth)
output-fields.comparison: the original-rule word recomputed beside the new-rule word over IDENTICAL bytes
